site-fort-canning-temasek: Hill-centre reference for archaeological activity across Fort Canning; the 1984 trench is not located by this point.
site-singapore-stone: Rocky Point river-mouth vicinity, using the documented present Fullerton landmark as reference. NLB's Bukit Larangan map account places the former stone near present Fullerton; this is not the museum or a survey of the destroyed rock.
site-longyamen: Documented western Keppel entrance reference. NLB and NParks identify the Labrador entrance; the medieval identification remains interpretive and the present replica is not an original rock.
site-johor-lama: Documented centre/reference point of Johor Lama mukim; not the surveyed original fort footprint.
site-lingga-daik: Documented Daik town-centre reference for the Lingga court; not a palace footprint.
site-penang: Documented George Town city-centre reference for the Penang settlement.
site-malacca: Documented Malacca city-centre reference for the regional settlement.
mahmud-iii-dies: Documented Daik town-centre reference for the ruler's Lingga court; no exact death chamber is asserted.
raffles-arrives: Documented commemorative landing-site reference behind Parliament House, identified by NLB. The fleet first anchored off St John's Island; this point represents the subsequent mainland visit, not the ships' anchorage or a certain 1819 landing spot.
preliminary-agreement-1819: North-bank Temenggong settlement vicinity, using the later Arts House site as the present reference. Roots' Padang history identifies the Temenggong's house in this open-space area; the exact signing place is unproved.
hussein-brought-from-riau: Documented Penyengat island/locality-centre reference for Hussein's Riau origin, supported by the Law Gazette historical account. The point is not an invented departure shore or ship position.
treaty-1819: Temenggong settlement/open-space vicinity, referenced by today's Arts House. NLB's On Paper guide explicitly says the treaty location is unknown; this is a source-backed vicinity marker, not a claim that this later building existed in 1819.
dutch-protest-1819: Documented Malacca city-centre reference for the Dutch regional context. This is a locality-level political marker, not the place where a particular protest letter was drafted.
farquhar-resident: Documented central-town district reference for the Singapore appointment; the exact office or appointment ceremony is not established.
site-temenggong-village: Roots' Padang history identifies the later Arts House open-space area with the Temenggong's settlement. Present building coordinate is a vicinity reference; the 1819 village extent is not reconstructed.
town-committee-1822: Documented central-town district reference for the planning committee's remit; no meeting-room position is claimed.
boat-quay-fill: Documented Boat Quay place-centre reference for the south-bank reclamation; not the centroid of a measured 1822 earthwork footprint.
convention-1823: Documented central-town district reference for the Singapore agreement; exact signing room is unproved.
site-telok-blangah: Documented Telok Blangah district-centre reference for the Temenggong's relocated settlement; the original residence footprint is not asserted.
site-kampong-glam-istana: Documented present Istana monument reference; distinguishes the later masonry building from Hussein's earlier establishment.
singapore-institution: Documented present Raffles City site reference for the former Bras Basah Institution. NLB's Singapore's First School identifies Raffles City as the old premises; not the present Bishan school.
anglo-dutch-treaty: Documented London city-centre reference for the treaty's signing locality; no signing-room coordinate is claimed.
crawfurd-treaty: Documented Singapore central-town district centre/reference. NLB's On Paper guide says the treaty signing location is unknown; a precise building is not inferred.
census-1824: Documented geographic centre of Singapore (Wikidata P5140), representing the island-wide return rather than an enumeration office.
straits-settlements-1826: Documented George Town city-centre reference for the initial Penang administrative seat; no exact founding-day ceremony is inferred.
capital-to-singapore: Documented central-town district reference for transfer of the Straits administrative seat, not a surveyed 1832 office footprint.
malacca-handover: Documented Malacca city-centre reference for the change in administration; no exact handover ceremony point is established.
naning-war: Documented Naning district reference point, used as its locality centre. The Wikidata point is unreferenced and is not a surveyed centroid or individual battlefield.
hong-kong-1841: Documented Victoria city-centre reference for British Hong Kong; not the exact 1841 landing or flagstaff position.
tanjong-pagar-dock: Documented Keppel/New Harbour locality reference for the dock development; not an exact early dock boundary.
crown-colony-1867: Documented central-town district reference for Singapore's administration, rather than an invented proclamation venue.
suez-1869: Documented Port Said city-centre reference for the canal's Mediterranean opening locality; no ceremonial yacht position or canal route is inferred.
first-amoy-junk: Documented river-mouth coordinate (the mouth-qualified P625 statement), representing the port of arrival. It is not a ship's reconstructed berth.
convicts-arrive: Documented Bras Basah district-centre reference for the convict establishment described in NLB's convict-labour history; not the brig's berth or a surveyed original prison footprint.
convict-transport-ends: Documented Bras Basah district-centre reference for the penal establishment; no exact place for the administrative termination decision is known.
chinese-protectorate: Documented Boat Quay locality-centre reference adjoining North Canal Road, where NLB locates the first Protectorate office. No shophouse number or later Havelock Road office is substituted.
indian-immigration-ordinance: Documented central-town district reference for colonial legislation applying across Singapore; no enactment-room location is inferred.
census-1871: Documented geographic centre of Singapore (P5140), representing the island-wide return rather than a census office.
site-raffles-institution: Documented present Raffles City reference for the former Bras Basah campus, identified by NLB; not the current Bishan campus.
site-chinatown: Documented Chinatown district-centre reference; not a measured boundary or a claim that the plan created settlement on a precise day.
site-kampong-glam: Documented Kampong Glam district-centre reference; the plan allocation and actual settlement are different matters.
site-serangoon-road: Documented core of the Serangoon/Little India locality: NHB's Little India trail describes the pre-1980 district core as centred on Tekka Market. The modern Tekka coordinate is a district-centre reference, not an 1823 building.
riots-1854: Documented Kampong Glam district-centre reference for the North Bridge Road town clashes described by NLB. Violence also spread to rural districts; the point is not a unique onset or casualty site.
telok-ayer-reclamation: Documented Raffles Place/Commercial Square locality-centre reference for the commercial waterfront. NLB's Land From Sand describes extension from Collyer Quay into Cecil Street and Telok Ayer; the point is not a measured reclamation centroid.
post-office-riots-1876: Documented Raffles Place commercial-district centre/reference for the Market Street disturbance. Lane Harris's source identifies the Chinese sub-post office at 81 Market Street and Philip/King Streets; the vanished address is not assigned an invented parcel point.
pangkor-1874: Documented Pangkor island/locality reference for the treaty; no vessel's position is reconstructed.
perak-war: Documented Pasir Salak locality centre/reference for Birch's killing and the war's origin; it does not represent every campaign site.
fms-1896: Documented Kuala Lumpur city-centre reference for the federal administrative seat; not a signing-room coordinate.
johor-treaty-1885: Documented London city-centre reference: the event's historical source locates the treaty signature in London, rather than at its former Johor orientation point.
labuan-to-ss: Documented Victoria/Labuan town-centre reference for the administrative transfer; no exact ceremony venue is claimed.
anglo-siamese-treaty: Documented Bangkok city-centre reference for the treaty locality, not an invented signing venue.
mutiny-1915: Documented Alexandra district-centre reference: NLB locates the regiment at Alexandra Barracks near Alexandra Road. The lost barracks' precise footprint remains unproved; Gillman Barracks, built later, is not substituted.
mutiny-executions-1915: Documented former Outram Prison reference, cross-checked with NLB's account of public executions outside its gates. The exact firing-squad spot or gate alignment is not surveyed.
kreta-ayer-1927: Documented Kreta Ayer district-centre reference for the police-station shooting; not an invented original station footprint.
census-1931: Documented geographic centre of Singapore (P5140), representing the island-wide census rather than an enumeration office.
dindings-to-perak: Documented Lumut town-centre reference for the Dindings administrative district and transfer; no boundary or cession ceremony is inferred from this point.
four-states-to-thailand: Documented Alor Setar city-centre reference representing Kedah, one of four transferred states. It is not the location of every transfer ceremony.
allied-raids-singapore: Documented Sembawang district-centre reference for the naval-base target of the first November 1944 raid. The operation covered other targets and months; the exact dry-dock caisson is not located here.
bahau-settlement: Documented Bahau town-centre reference for the settlement's vicinity. NLB says the camp was five miles from town; the town point must not be read as the camp footprint.
endau-settlement: Documented Endau town-centre reference for the wider agricultural-settlement locality; the original settlement plot is not surveyed.
bma-1945: Documented City Hall reference for the September surrender/return chapter anchor. This does not put the proclamation's August signature at City Hall or resolve the precise first day of island-wide control.
colony-of-singapore-1946: Documented geographic centre (P5140), representing an island-wide constitutional change; not an invented ceremony venue.
malayan-union: Documented Kuala Lumpur city-centre reference for the Union's administrative seat; not a measured proclamation venue.
umno-founded: Documented Istana Besar building reference for the founding congress's Johor venue, as identified by the institutional chronology; not a surveyed seat within its hall.
federation-1948: Documented Kuala Lumpur city-centre reference for the federal administrative seat; not a surveyed signature or ceremony location.
election-1948: Documented geographic centre (P5140), representing voting across Singapore; no single polling station represents all contests.
emergency-1948: Documented Sungai Siput town-centre reference for the Perak district where the June plantation killings precipitated Emergency declarations, as NLB describes. The exact estates and each declaration venue are not surveyed.
hertogh-riots: Documented Kampong Glam district-centre reference for the town-area unrest; NLB also identifies court-area clashes. This marker is not asserted as the first clash point or as proof that unrest began at Sultan Mosque.
election-1955: Documented geographic centre (P5140), representing the island-wide election rather than a particular polling station.
marshall-resigns: Documented Assembly House reference for the chief minister's legislative context; no exact resignation handover room is inferred.
school-riots-1956: Documented Chinese High School reference, one of the occupied campuses named by NHB. Chung Cheng High and wider disturbances are also involved; this is not the sole riot site.
merdeka-1957: Documented Stadium Merdeka building/site reference, the independence celebration venue identified by Arkib Negara Malaysia. The exact ceremonial platform is not surveyed.
citizenship-1957: Documented Assembly House reference for Singapore legislation; exact assent or commencement venue is not inferred.
election-1959: Documented geographic centre (P5140), representing the island-wide election rather than one polling place.
self-government-1959: Documented City Hall reference: NHB's Jubilee Walk booklet places Lee's 3 June self-government mass rally on its steps. This does not turn the island-wide constitutional change into a measured platform footprint.
first-cabinet-1959: Documented City Hall building reference for the 5 June oath ceremony identified in NAS records; exact room position is not surveyed.
yusof-ishak-1959: Documented City Hall building reference for the December inauguration/public symbols locality; not a new surveyed ceremony footprint.
tunku-proposal-1961: SLA OneMap current The Adelphi site reference at 1 Coleman Street, where NLB locates the demolished Adelphi Hotel. Arkib Negara identifies the 27 May luncheon venue there. It is a present site coordinate, not the exact former dining room.
barisan-sosialis-1961: Documented geographic centre (P5140), representing the party's Singapore formation; founding, registration and individual premises are not collapsed into an invented venue.
referendum-1962: Documented geographic centre (P5140), representing voting throughout Singapore rather than one polling place.
brunei-revolt: Documented Brunei Town (today Bandar Seri Begawan) city-centre reference for the uprising; not a unique engagement site.
coldstore-1963: Documented geographic centre (P5140), representing arrests across Singapore; not a particular detainee's home or police station.
malaysia-agreement: Documented London city-centre reference for the 9 July signature locality, confirmed by the UN treaty text; no signing-room coordinate is claimed.
malaysia-day-1963: Documented Stadium Merdeka site reference for the Malaysia proclamation ceremony identified by Arkib Negara Malaysia; not a surveyed platform or the venue of every simultaneous state ceremony.
konfrontasi-begins: Documented Kuching city-centre reference for the Borneo theatre of confrontation. This regional marker is not the Jakarta policy-declaration venue or an individual incursion site.
malaysia-election-1964: Documented Kuala Lumpur city-centre reference for the federal political context of a nationwide election; not one polling station.
race-riots-july-1964: Documented Kallang district-centre reference: NLB places the first reported clashes near Kallang Road and Kampong Soo Poo. It does not establish an exact street-corner onset position.
race-riots-september-1964: Present Geylang Serai Market as a documented locality-centre reference for the Geylang Serai area. NHB defines the locality around this market and describes the market as its social/economic centre. This is not a claim for the exact trishaw killing site, the opposite Changi Market, or the footprint of the former1964 market.
independence-agreement-1965: Documented Kuala Lumpur city-centre reference for the separation negotiations and signature locality; the exact residence room is not surveyed.
separation-1965: Documented City Hall reference: NHB's Jubilee Walk account says the Proclamation of Singapore was issued from Lee's office there. The radio reading and Malaysian parliamentary vote occurred elsewhere; no broadcast studio or exact office desk is inferred.
first-cabinet-1965: Documented City Hall government-office reference for the cabinet reorganisation. NHB identifies the Prime Minister's and ministries' offices here; the contemporary source reports an announcement, not a fresh collective oath. No exact meeting room is inferred.
first-president-1965: Documented Parliament House reference for the 22 December statutory change, as described in the legal source; not an invented new presidential oath venue.
